patch.value: Linear-space divide-and-conquer diff, for an absolute memory ceiling the band bound cannot give

The banded trace from pm-vcs-ze24 bounds each snapshot to the 2d plus 1 reachable diagonals, which turns the trace from d times combined width into d squared. That is a real and provable win, but it is a relative one. The trace is still quadratic in the edit distance, so two ten-thousand-line files with nothing in common still hold roughly 1.6 gibibytes of live Int32 storage against the 3.2 gibibytes the full-width version paid. Raised by CodeRabbit on pull request 21, which correctly observed that comparing the banded total against the rectangular total is an inequality holding for every input and therefore bounds nothing in absolute terms.

The diff computes an edit script for two ten-thousand-line files with no common lines inside a fixed memory ceiling that does not grow with the edit distance, using the linear-space divide-and-conquer form of the algorithm in which the middle snake is located from a forward and a reverse pass and the two halves are recursed into. Edit scripts stay byte-identical to the current banded implementation across the existing randomized and edge-shaped equivalence corpus. The pathological ten-thousand-line case runs in the default suite rather than behind an opt-in environment variable, because it no longer depends on the runner having gibibytes free.

value.text: Raised by CodeRabbit on pull request 21 with the arithmetic spelled out: at size 10000 the edit distance is 20000, so the banded total is (20001) squared equals 400040001 Int32 entries, about 1.6 gibibytes, and every one of the 20001 snapshots stays reachable until the backtrack returns. The reviewer also noted the only budget assertion compared the banded total against the rectangular total, an inequality true for every input. Both points were correct. The test now asserts the budget in bytes against the closed form and the full ten-thousand-line size is opt-in behind PM_VCS_DIFF_PATHOLOGICAL_SIZE, so a routine run no longer depends on 1.6 gibibytes being free.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Linear-space middle-snake engine added to engine/diff.ts: forward and reverse furthest-reaching passes locate the middle snake (paper-faithful extraction - the pass that detects the overlap reports its own last snake, reverse search in minimized-y space), the two halves recurse, and reported segments carry one edit edge plus their diagonal run. diffLines routes by combined width via exported linearSpaceDiffWidthThreshold=4096: below it the banded greedy engine answers byte-identically to before (worst-case trace ~67MB there), above it the linear engine answers, so peak memory no longer grows with edit distance anywhere. Measured pathological case (10k+10k lines, no common line, distance 20000): runs in the default suite in ~1.7-2.5s at 40006 peak live Int32 entries (~156KB) against the 1,600,160,004-byte banded budget - four orders of magnitude less. Differential testing during development caught two real defects (an overlap-extraction that assumed frontier spans were common substrings, producing invalid scripts; a sentinel-type mismatch that degenerated the search) before settling; final fuzz over 38k randomized trials across alphabets 1-8 found zero invalid scripts and zero distance mismatches vs the band. Note: byte-identity of scripts between engines holds only where the shortest script is essentially unique; on tie-heavy inputs both emit equally short but differently tied scripts, so the routing contract pins byte-identity for all corpus-sized inputs (verified by test) and optimality equality for every input. Revert-proof checks: threshold=MAX_SAFE_INTEGER fails the wide-routing test; threshold=0 fails both corpus byte-identity tests including the pre-existing ze24 differential. Gates: build ok; npm test 606/606; coverage 100/100/100/100 via c8 --all --100 (engine/diff.ts fully covered); docstring gate 33 files / 159 declarations; ./node_modules/.bin/pm health --strict-exit exit 0.

patch.value: Hybrid engine shipped: banded below width 4096 (byte-identical legacy behavior), linear-space middle-snake divide-and-conquer above it with a fixed memory ceiling proven by the default-suite 10k pathological test; optimality equivalence to the band fuzz-verified across 38k randomized inputs.
